advisory.title: Request smuggling through malformed chunked request trailers
advisory.description:
The HTTP/1 chunked decoder accepts a bare line feed after the final chunk as
the start of a trailer instead of rejecting the malformed request.

When an upstream proxy reuses a connection and either pipelines the requests or
does not take steps to validate the chunked stream, the decoder can consume the
next request's headers as trailer data. It can then parse that request's body as
a new request. An attacker can use this difference in request parsing to bypass
access controls enforced by a proxy or web application firewall.

Upgrade to actix-http 3.20.2 or later.

advisory.title: Large-window Brotli bodies bypass decompression memory limits
advisory.description:
With the `compress-brotli` feature enabled, the decoder accepts the non-standard
large-window Brotli format. A crafted stream can cause its internal buffer to
grow to about 1 GiB before the decoded output reaches the configured size limit.
An 850-byte request can cause this allocation, and concurrent requests can
exhaust process or host memory.

Actix Web enables Brotli support by default. Applications that read request
bodies through `Bytes`, `String`, `Json`, or `Form` can be affected even when
extractor size limits are configured. The allocation occurs before the handler
runs, so authentication performed in the handler does not prevent it.

Upgrade to actix-http 3.20.3 or later. As a workaround, reject requests with
`Content-Encoding: br` at a reverse proxy or in middleware before body
extraction, or disable the `compress-brotli` feature throughout the dependency
graph.

advisory.title: Unbounded decompression can exhaust memory and CPU resources
advisory.description:
The `encoding::Decoder` stream can expand compressed input into a large output
buffer before a caller can enforce its body size limit. An attacker who controls
a compressed request or response can cause excessive memory allocation and CPU
use, resulting in denial of service.

This affects applications that decode untrusted gzip, deflate, Brotli, or Zstandard
bodies with the corresponding compression feature enabled.

Upgrade to actix-http 3.20.1 or later and configure `Decoder::limit()` when using
the decoder directly. Actix Web users must also upgrade to actix-web 4.18.2 or
later so that extractors pass their limits to the decoder.

advisory.title: Potential request smuggling capabilities due to lack of input validation
advisory.description:
Affected versions of this crate did not properly detect invalid requests that could allow HTTP/1 request smuggling (HRS) attacks when running alongside a vulnerable front-end proxy server. This can result in leaked internal and/or user data, including credentials, when the front-end proxy is also vulnerable.

Popular front-end proxies and load balancers already mitigate HRS attacks so it is recommended that they are also kept up to date; check your specific set up. You should upgrade even if the front-end proxy receives exclusively HTTP/2 traffic and connects to the back-end using HTTP/1; several downgrade attacks are known that can also expose HRS vulnerabilities.

advisory.title: Use-after-free in BodyStream due to lack of pinning
advisory.description:
Affected versions of this crate did not require the buffer wrapped in `BodyStream` to be pinned,
but treated it as if it had a fixed location in memory. This may result in a use-after-free.
 
The flaw was corrected by making the trait `MessageBody` require `Unpin`
and making `poll_next()` function accept `Pin<&mut Self>` instead of `&mut self`.
